sentences.text: These Criminal Revision Petitions are arising out of the common judgment, hence, taken up together for disposal.
2. The ranks of the parties in the Trial Court will be considered henceforth, for convenience.
3. It is the case of the prosecution that, initially a complaint came to be registered by the complainant before the Magistrate.
Later, it was referred to the jurisdictional police for investigation and for report.

4. As per the averments of the complaint, the representatives of the Company viz., 'Preet Tractors'
had been to T.B.Gollarahatti and met the farmers of the village and explained the performance and consistency of the tractor for the purpose of promoting the sale of tractors.

Like wise, they approached the complainant and instructed him that they would make necessary arrangements to purchase tractor by arranging loan from their known bank and accordingly, took the complainant to the bank and also took some signatures on the papers pertaining to the loan.
As per the averments of the complaint, the complainant had applied two loans one is for agricultural purpose and another one is for the purpose of purchasing the tractor.
The complainant said to have received agricultural loan of Rs.1,00,000/-, however, he did not get any loan sanctioned to purchase the Tractor.
Though he approached the officials for the loan, he was advised to wait for 2 to 3 months.
Even after lapse of 2 to 3 months, he did not get any information regarding sanction of loan to purchase the Tractor.
However, on 11.06.2008, he received notice from the bank and asked him to pay the installment for having obtained loan to purchase the tractor.

Being aggrieved by the said notice, the complainant explained the bank manager that he did not receive any loan to purchase the tractor, however, the bank manager insisted the complainant to pay the instalments and he told that as per the documents the complainant got sanctioned the loan to purchase the tractor.

5. It is further stated in the complaint that the complainant after having obtained the details about the tractor which allegedly purchased by him, approached the RTO and obtained documents pertaining to the tractor which the bank authority allegedly sanctioned the loan.
To his surprise, the said documents were standing in the name of different persons.
The complainant after having learnt that he has been cheated by the accused, filed a private complaint to take necessary action against the accused.
It was referred to the jurisdictional police for investigation.
The jurisdictional police after completion of investigation, submitted charge sheet.
6. Heard Sri. Rajendra Reddy, learned counsel for accused No.1 / petitioner in Crl.R.P.No.705/2020, Sri.

Veeranna G.Tigadi, learned counsel for accused Nos.4 & 5/petitioners in Crl.R.P.No.672/2020, Sri. Sudhanva, learned counsel for accused No.6 in Crl.R.P.No.845/2020,
Sri.

R.Shashidhar, learned counsel for accused No.2 in Crl.R.P.No.296/2021 and Sri. Rahul Rai.K,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.

7. It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioners that the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court and the Appellate Court are perverse, illegal and against to the evidence on record.
Therefore, the said judgment is required to be set aside.
8. It is the submission of learned counsel for accused No.1 that the prosecution has failed to prove the involvement of accused No.1 either in fabricating the documents or forging or cheating PW.1.
Ex.P16 is the delivery challan which discloses the name of P.W.1.
The said documents itself indicates that P.W.1 had purchased tractor and trailer and the same had been delivered to P.W.1 on 10.05.2006.
Such being the fact, he cannot make such allegations against the accused that he did not receive the tractor.
The Courts below have failed to consider Ex.P16-document properly and passed the impugned judgment.

C.Manjunatha vs State By Kote Police Station on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117903916/

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove that accused No.1 has fabricated the documents for the purpose of cheating PW.1.
Therefore, the conviction in respect of the aforesaid offences are required to be set aside.
Submission of learned counsels for accused Nos. 4, 5 and 6.
All these accused are relating to State Bank of India, taken up together for consideration.

10. It is the submission of learned counsels for accused Nos. 4, 5 and 6 that they are the manager,
deputy manager of SBI, Chitradurga Branch respectively and accused No.6 is the field Officer of the said bank.

It is further submitted that even though the prosecution has not proved the nexus between accused Nos.1 to 3 with these accused, the Courts below have convicted accused Nos. 5 to 6,
opined that these accused are colluded with other accused and stated to have sanctioned loan to purchase the tractor in the name of P.W.1.
However, the said tractor was not delivered to P.W.1 is baseless and false and the said findings are against to the evidence on record.
It is further submitted that the evidence of P.W.1 discloses that he had been to the bank and signed certain documents relating to loan and went away from the bank.
It is needless to say that as per the procedure of the bank and also as per the quotation produced by the loanee, the sanctioned loan had been disbursed directly to the dealer.
The banker have produced relevant documents to the jurisdictional police not only for having sanctioned the loan but also cheque which was disbursed to the dealer.

11. It is further submitted that as per the allegations of the complainant, the tractor's registration number, chassis number and engine number have been fabricated and created fake RC book and produced the same to the bank for the purpose of availing loan.
According to P.W.1, the delivery - 10 - challan which is marked as Ex.P16 contained the tractor, chassis and engine number which belong to the tractor of Nijalingappa as per Ex.P7.
The registration number of the tractor alleged to have sanctioned loan belongs to the tractor of Basappa as per Ex.P8.
Neither Ex.P16 nor any other documents contained the signature of these accused.

Therefore, it cannot be said that accused Nos.
4, 5 and 6 have fabricated or created bogus or fake documents for the purpose of availing loan.
Therefore, the conviction recorded by the Courts below against the accused are required to be set aside.
Submission of learned counsel for accused No.2 12.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for accused No.2 that accused No.2 being a Manager of Tractor showroom has neither signed any quotation nor any documents relating to the Tractor stated to have been purchased by PW.1.
The prosecution has failed to prove the nexus between PW.1 and accused No.2.
The Trial Court and the Appellate Court have failed to appreciate the evidence properly and recorded the conviction.
Therefore the conviction against accused No.2 requires to be set aside.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the respective parties pray to allow the petitions.

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader for State vehemently justified the judgment and conviction passed by the Trial Court and its confirmation order passed by the Appellate Court and submitted that accused Nos. 1 to 6 have colluded with each other in order to cheat PW1.

It is further submitted that they have created fake documents like RC book and delivery challan by mentioning the fake chassis and engine numbers and also the fake registration number and stated to have sanctioned loan.
In fact, P.W.1 is not the beneficiary of the said loan.
14. It is further submitted that, in fact, P.W.1 did not get any information regarding sanction of loan or purchase of tractor till he received the notice from the bank for payment of installments.

15. It is further submitted that prosecution has proved the case, not only through the oral evidence,
but also, by producing the documentary evidence namely Ex.P6, Ex.P7, Ex.P8, Ex.P9 and Ex.P16.
Therefore, the Trial Court and Appellate Court have concluded that the accused are found guilty for the aforesaid offenses.
The findings of the Courts below in recording the conviction are proper and there are no - 12 - infirmities or errors in the said findings.
Hence, interference may not be warranted.
Making such submissions, the learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petitions.

16. Having heard the submission of the respective parties and also perused the findings of the Courts below, now it is relevant to refer the evidence of all the witnesses in order to arrive at a conclusion as to whether any errors have been committed by the Courts below in recording the conviction.
17. PW1 is the complainant.

According to him, some representatives of the Company of accused Nos.
1 to 3 had approached him and induced him to purchase the tractor of their Company and took his signatures to the loan papers and thereafter, assured him that they would get loan sanctioned and also assured him that they would hand over the tractor.
As per their advice, he had affixed his signatures and handed over some papers to the representatives.

Further, P.W.1 deposed in his evidence that whenever he enquired the officials of the tractor Company regarding sanction of loan to purchase the tractor, he was advised to wait for two to three months.
. It is further noticed in the evidence of P.W.1 that he kept quiet for a longer period believing that loan has not been sanctioned.
However, on 11.06.2008, he received a notice from the bank and asked him to pay installments for having borrowed loan to purchase the tractor.

When P.W.1 enquired about the transaction, he learnt that officials of the tractor Company and the bank officials colluded with each other and fabricated some documents relating to the some other tractors and created fake RC book and delivery challan and obtained loan as if, they have delivered the tractor to C.Manjunatha vs State By Kote Police Station on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117903916/
7 P.W.1.
19.

sentences.text: On careful analysis of the documents especially, Ex.P16-Delivery Challan which is standing in the name of P.W.1, it contains certain details of the tractor said to be delivered to P.W.1.
However, the details of the tractor mentioned in Ex.P16 relating to Nijalingaappa.
Similarly, the registration number mentioned in the RC book produced to the bank standing in the name of Basappa.
20. No doubt, the RC book, copy of insurance and delivery challan appeared to be fabricated for the purpose of availing loan.
However, Ex.P16-delivery challan bears the signature of Ravi who is arrayed as accused No.1.
It is needless - 14 - to say that he was the tractor dealer and accused No.2 was the manager of the tractor showroom.

On reading of both oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that accused Nos. 1 and 2 have created Ex.P16 by mentioning the fake chassis and engine numbers and also created a fake RC book and insurance copy for the purpose of availing loan.
21. On careful reading of evidence of P.W.1, he admitted in his evidence that he had been to the bank to execute certain documents relating to both crop and purchase loan.
When such being the fact, it cannot be said that accused Nos. 4 to 6 have created fake documents to sanction loan.
In fact, these accused were not aware about the chassis and engine numbers mentioned in Ex.P16 which were fake and bogus.
Merely because P.W.1 has been cheated by the officials of the tractor Company, the bank officials cannot be dragged into the case without any evidence regarding their involvement.

It is needless to say that the prosecution has not produced any document to show that the same bank officials have sanctioned the loan to the other two persons, namely, Nijalingappa and Basappal to purchase the tractors.
Therefore, the conviction in respect of accused Nos. 4, 5 and 6, in my considered opinion is - 15 - not proper and cannot be sustained.
Hence, the conviction against accused Nos.4 to 6 in respect of aforesaid offences has to be set aside.

22. In the light of the observation made above, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER i) The petitions are allowed in-part.

ii) The judgment of conviction and order on sentence dated 27.01.2020 passed in C.C.No.1028/2011 by the II Addl. Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Chitradurga and the judgment and order dated 14.09.2020 passed in Crl.A.Nos. 19, 20 and 25 of 2020 by the I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Chitradurga are set aside in respect C.Manjunatha vs State By Kote Police Station on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117903916/
8 of accused Nos. 4, 5 and 6.

The prosecution has failed to prove the nexus between PW.1 and accused No.2.
Therefore, the Trial Court and Appellate Court have concluded that the accused are found guilty for the aforesaid offenses.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Trial Court and the Appellate Court have failed to appreciate the evidence properly and recorded the conviction.
Therefore the conviction against accused No.2 requires to be set aside.
The findings of the Courts below in recording the conviction are proper and there are no - 12 - infirmities or errors in the said findings.
